title: Repository coverage claims form a non-interchangeable evidence lattice
durable_memory: A repository search result is evidence about the inspected search surface, not evidence of repository-wide absence. Provenance may be classified unlocated only after the declared coverage includes every accessible ref and the reachable commit graph, with immutable traversal evidence retained.

observed: The active queue requires exhaustive branch inventory or equivalent history traversal before M-004, M-005, and M-006 may be classified unlocated.
The GitHub code-search connector returned no indexed result for M-004 in this run.
An empty branch-search query returned no branch objects and therefore did not establish a branch inventory.
inferred: No-result indexed search is compatible with absence, incomplete indexing, inaccessible refs, unsupported query behavior, or namespace mismatch.
Coverage evidence must be retained independently from the candidate provenance objects it evaluates.
proposed: All continuity provenance artifacts should declare one coverage class from this lattice and reject promotion from a weaker class to repository_exhaustive without immutable traversal evidence.
superseded: Treating a no-result code search as proof that an artifact never existed.
Describing an unspecified repository search as exhaustive.
unresolved: The complete accessible ref inventory for the repository.
The originating immutable objects for M-004, M-005, and M-006.

coverage_lattice.meaning: One or more indexed search queries were executed.
Declared paths on the default branch were inspected.
A named, incomplete set of refs and reachable objects was traversed.
Every ref returned by an authenticated inventory was traversed, but graph-completeness or hidden-ref limits remain unresolved.
Every accessible ref and reachable commit was traversed with retained inventory, pagination, commit identities, and tool-limit evidence.

required_evidence: authenticated ref inventory with pagination completeness
immutable snapshot time and repository identity
reachable commit traversal for every inventoried ref
declared handling of tags, pull-request refs, deleted refs, forks, and inaccessible objects
digest or immutable locator for retained traversal outputs
fail_closed_conditions: candidate identified only by suffix collision

contradiction_resolved: A search can be complete relative to its declared query while remaining incomplete relative to repository history. Query completeness and repository completeness are separate claims.
falsification_route: Falsify this rule by producing a documented GitHub guarantee that a no-result indexed code search covers every accessible ref and all reachable historical objects, including unindexed or deleted-path history; absent such a guarantee, the weaker coverage classification remains required.
next_action: Implement an authenticated ref-and-commit inventory artifact, then apply this lattice to M-004, M-005, and M-006 candidate adjudication.
